limits: No real hardware setting, PBO effect or stability measurement has been verified.
Only Shimada family 1Ah/model 08h at PCI 1022:153a/BDF 0 is admitted for native PM capture. Nonzero firmware length must match an exact supported version.

Native capture checks identity, reported length, 64-bit address range, transfer acknowledgement and metadata after all reads. Failed transfers/reads/rechecks publish no buffer. Freshness, atomicity and physical mapping remain unverified.
Fmax still has acknowledgement only. Rails has only an offline bounded encoding preview; physical targets and its two-command transaction remain unverified.
Original dynamic-memory and EC dynamic-EDC paths remain research-only. Their original Applied/return behavior is not proof of firmware acceptance or effective hardware changes.
Per-core/CCD PM telemetry layout remains unresolved. Other AMD profiles, broader native PM transport, Intel server controls and board-specific settings remain incomplete.
EL7 means Oracle Linux 7.9 x86_64. Windows/macOS validate the portable core, not a full application port.
QEMU verifies module integration only; Secure Boot and actual register settings were not tested.

original_replay.scope: Full pinned address/transfer and conversion helper instructions. Explicit synthetic PM object, PCI reads/writes, global flags, is_am5_es, locks and sleep. Read failure returns a synthetic FFFFFFFF sentinel. No real firmware, constructor selection or electrical contract is certified.

calibration.scope: Original constructor then a second call with explicit calibration flag reset and synthetic alternating MMIO values. Observe at most 128 calibration reads; completed cases compare original mode-4 layout with the earlier calibrated-state fixture. Not hardware topology or a valid firmware layout.
observations: After explicitly resetting the calibration flags, completed original calibration paths changed only members CD8/CDC/CE0 and left all core/CCD read groups unchanged in the two sampled version/topology combinations.

730204 with synthetic 2 CCDs still has 22 words outside the public table; 731004 with synthetic 16 CCDs still has 176 overlapping core/CCD words. These are synthetic conflict examples, not certified topology/version pairings.

An invalid first value branches around the 30-count check; observation stops before read 129 with calibration incomplete. This proves the 30-count check is not a global scan bound, not that every input loops forever.
A quiet NaN first value reaches dispatch after two reads. Calibration completion is not a validity check for firmware data.

All ten REA functions were matched to original ELF offsets, full symbol bytes and Capstone disassembly. The PIE analysis address is original offset plus 0x100000; mixed PCI calling-convention pseudocode does not reliably preserve arguments.

Original start_monitor/address functions force response to 1 without reading completion. Synthetic PCI write/read failures do not terminate these linear paths. The 32-bit address function releases its lock before its final data read; the 64-bit function reads both address halves while locked.
These experiments seed a declared synthetic object. They do not prove which constructor/caller selects these offsets or flags on real hardware. Core/CCD layout conflicts are unchanged.

Original cal_vid_from_raw/cal_raw_from_vid use SVI3 arithmetic only when (AM5_ES or GRANITE) and not SHIMADA and not GPT. Enabling SHIMADA therefore selects SVI2 arithmetic, even with AM5_ES/GRANITE set.

The independently replayed original rails setter uses the 245 mV/5 mV 9-bit formula. The general conversion helper disagrees and cannot be reused as the rails protocol. Neither proves physical rail mapping or a safe writable voltage range.

New native PM requires exact version and nonzero matching firmware length, a bounded 64-bit physical range, acknowledged one-shot transfer and unchanged metadata after reading. It publishes no buffer on transport/recheck failure and requests no tuning setting.
No hardware acceptance, atomic sample, fresh sample, physical socket mapping or full original restoration is claimed.

post_build_static_review.scope: Static follow-up using archived REA evidence plus full original symbol bytes. No additional cloud REA run or new test count is claimed.
observations: Rd_MMIO adds the unsigned 64-bit byte offset to the 64-bit object base at +18h, using wrapping machine arithmetic. It performs no fourfold scaling, stride correction, masking or bounds check.
The mixed-ABI call passes the resulting address in RCX. The wrapper explicitly zero-extends EAX before returning, preserving only the 32-bit word.
Read_MMIO selects the original kernel path when MY_KMOD_LOADED is true; otherwise it requests a four-byte devmem mapping. This does not prove a valid base or PM buffer.
The kernel reader sends opcode 0Ch, the same absolute address and a 96-byte request. It ignores the write result and waits for the entire completion word to equal one, with no timeout.
The existing NGU instruction fixture contains this same generic wrapper and already exercises base-plus-offset reads; this static follow-up does not add to the cloud test count.
This rejects a hidden stride conversion in the wrapper as an explanation for the PM core/CCD conflicts. Wrong base selection, unknown firmware layout and physical mapping remain unresolved.
